# Basic Statistics {.unnumbered}

This part of the book is a short refresher of the basic statistics you have probably met in earlier courses: how to summarize the centre and the spread of a list of numbers, how to describe the association between two variables with a correlation, and how to compare two groups with the t-test and the Wilcoxon test. It is meant to be read, not studied as a new topic: the course refers to these chapters whenever a concept such as the standard deviation or the correlation coefficient is used, so that you can check its definition quickly. The chapters use the same `behdslabs` datasets as the rest of the book. The ideas behind statistical inference, such as standard errors, confidence intervals and p-values, are explained in [Part 2](https://intro-to-behds.github.io/behdsbook-part-2/) of this book. If you want a fuller treatment, several excellent books are freely available online: Danielle Navarro's [*Learning Statistics with R*](https://learningstatisticswithr.com/), written for psychology students; Russell Poldrack's [*Statistical Thinking for the 21st Century*](https://statsthinking21.github.io/statsthinking21-core-site/); and Daniël Lakens' [*Improving Your Statistical Inferences*](https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/), which focuses on p-values, effect sizes and confidence intervals. Each chapter ends with pointers to the relevant sections.

This part is original material written for this book; it is not part of Irizarry's *Introduction to Data Science*.
